CANONICAL_NAME.value: TinySTM -- a lightweight word-based software transactional memory (Felber, Fetzer, Riegel, Marlier; 2007-)

VERSION.value: github.com/patrickmarlier/tinystm master as of 2026-09-12 (commit in hashes; 1.0.5 lineage)

value.lineage: Software transactional memory (Shavit & Touitou 1995) as the research lineage that competed with lock-based concurrency in the multicore decade: TinySTM (2007, Univ. Neuchatel / TU Dresden) uses time-based validation (Riegel), encounter- or commit-time locking, and ships micro-benchmarks (bank, intset) that count aborts/commits. The human record: STM lost the mainstream to fine-grained locks and lock-free structures, survived in Haskell/Clojure and Intel TSX -- a partly SUPERSEDED design, preserved.

HUMAN_PROBLEM.value: composable atomic memory updates without locks

value.built_to: let threads compose memory operations into atomic transactions that abort and retry on conflict instead of holding locks
value.pressure: contention (conflicting transactions abort), memory reordering, the cost of validation
value.success_means: the bank's total balance is invariant under any interleaving; aborts are bounded and retried

value.pressure: resource contention, competing writers, retry cost
value.failure_condition: abort storms under high contention (livelock-like) or a validation bug that commits a conflicting transaction
